caption: What if you were an emperor penguin for a day? You'd be the biggest penguin alive, up to about 1.2 metres tall and 45 kg. You'd breed in the Antarctic winter, when temperatures can drop to around -50 °C and winds hit 200 km/h. Mum lays a single egg, hands it to you, and walks off to the sea to feed. You balance that egg on your feet under a warm fold of skin for 65 to 75 days. By the time the chick hatches, you've gone about four months without eating and lost nearly half your body weight. Thousands of dads huddle and shuffle so everyone takes a turn on the freezing edge. Then you dive for dinner, as deep as 564 metres, the deepest dive recorded for any bird. That's nearly 8 Qutub Minars. India studies Antarctica from its Maitri and Bharati stations. Plot twist: if the chick hatches before Mum returns, Dad feeds it a milky goo made in his throat. Could YOU go 4 months without food? 👇
